extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling restriction/election/traverse, claims withdrawn, rejoinder, and related examiner actions under MPEP §821 (restriction in applications; double patenting). Covers form paragraphs, timing, and patentability/ double-patenting consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make restriction requirement final after traversal if still proper
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon reconsideration, the examiner is still of the opinion that restriction is proper, the examiner should maintain the restriction requirement and make it final in the next Office action. See MPEP § 803.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should reply to the reasons or arguments advanced by applicant in the traverse. Form paragraph 8.25 should be used to make a restriction requirement final. If the requirement is made final, the claims to the nonelected invention should be clearly indicated as being withdrawn from consideration (use form paragraph 8.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.25 — Answer to Arguments With Traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard wording acknowledging applicant's election with traverse and stating traversal grounds and why not persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert elected invention in bracket 1; summarize traversal grounds in bracket 3; insert reasons why traversal not persuasive in bracket 4. Use this paragraph when making restriction final after a traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: If requirement made final indicate withdrawn nonelected claims using form paragraph 8.05
rubrics_metrics.description: When a restriction requirement is made final, nonelected claims must be shown as withdrawn from further consideration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.142(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.05 wording identifies withdrawn claim and whether it is an --invention-- or --species-- and shows applicant retained right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144. Use this to preserve the petition record.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reconsideration shows restriction improper, withdraw and act on merits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner, upon reconsideration, is of the opinion that the requirement for restriction is improper in whole or in part, he or she should clearly state in the next Office action that the requirement for restriction is withdrawn in whole or in part, specify which groups have been reinstated, and give an action on the merits of all the claims directed to the elected invention and any invention reinstated with the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit reinstatement information and proceed to substantive examination of reinstated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.03 — In condition for allowance; non-elected claims withdrawn with traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for presence of nonelected claim(s) with traverse, applicant is given TWO MONTHS to cancel noted claims or take other action (37 CFR 1.144).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to act will be treated as authorization to cancel the noted claims by Examiner's Amendment and pass the case to issue. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted since application will be passed to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timing under 37 CFR 1.144 and effect at appeal/allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition under 37 CFR 1.144 must be filed not later than appeal (on or before the date the notice of appeal is filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is ready for allowance on or after the date of the notice of appeal and no petition has been filed, the examiner should cancel nonelected claims not eligible for rejoinder by examiner's amendment and call attention to 37 CFR 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election without traverse treated as final election
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the initial requirement is not traversed (either expressly or by virtue of an incomplete reply), the examiner should take appropriate action on the elected claims including determining whether the restriction requirement should be withdrawn in whole or in part. Form paragraphs 8.25.01 or 8.25.02 should be used to acknowledge the election without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is incomplete (not distinctly and specifically pointing out supposed errors), treat as election without traverse (MPEP § 818.01(a)); use 8.25.02 for incomplete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.06 — Claims stand withdrawn without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] withdrawn from further consideration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.142(b) as being drawn to a nonelected invention/species; election made without traverse in reply filed on [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert --invention-- or --species-- in bracket 2. When applicant has not retained right to petition and the application is otherwise ready for allowance, claims to nonelected inventions (except eligible for rejoinder) may be canceled by examiner’s amendment and application passed to issue; use form paragraph 8.07 in that situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.07 — Ready for allowance; non-elected claims withdrawn without traverse (cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application in condition for allowance except for presence of nonelected claims directed to nonelected invention without traverse; the claims may be canceled and prosecution passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate identification (invention(s) or species). Note that nonelected species and inventions eligible for rejoinder should be rejoined; claims not eligible for rejoinder may only be canceled by examiner’s amendment when cancellation is expressly authorized by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims added after an Office action (original presentation) — 37 CFR 1.145
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims added by amendment following action by examiner and drawn to an invention other than the one previously claimed should be treated under 37 CFR 1.145; applicant will be required to restrict to the invention previously claimed if the amendment is entered, subject to reconsideration and review under §§ 1.143 and 1.144.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.04 (Election by Original Presentation) to explain why newly submitted claim is directed to independent/distinct invention. Applicant must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in restriction to preserve right to petition. Traversal must be timely; failure to timely traverse results in loss of right to petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: If applicant traverses on non-patentable-distinctness grounds, submit evidence or admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Should applicant traverse on the ground that the inventions are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit evidence or identify such evidence now of record showing the inventions to be obvious variants or clearly admit on the record that this is the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner finds one invention unpatentable, the evidence or admission may be used in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of the other invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot cancel withdrawn claims without applicant authorization after amendment adds new invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner finds all elected claims allowable following the amendment that added claims drawn to a new invention, the examiner cannot cancel the withdrawn claims without obtaining the applicant's express authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may obtain express authorization via interview; if not obtained, issue Ex parte Quayle action requiring cancellation. In reply applicant can cancel withdrawn claims or traverse; if traverse examiner must reconsider election by original presentation and address applicant's arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment canceling all elected claims and presenting only nonelected claims is non-responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered; such an amendment is nonresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify applicant using form paragraph 8.26. Examiners should correctly designate this as a non-responsive amendment (not a notice of non-compliant amendment). May use PTOL-90 with form paragraph 8.26 to create a notice of non-responsive amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.26 — Canceled elected claims, non-responsive; shortened reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment canceling all elected claims and presenting only nonelected claims is non-responsive and has not been entered. Applicant is given TWO (2) MONTHS to supply omission or correction to avoid abandonment; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) ARE AVAILABLE but cannot carry reply date beyond statutory six-month maximum (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this paragraph for AE (accelerated examination) applications; use form paragraph 8.26.AE instead. Practice not applicable where provisional election of single species/group was made under MPEP §803.02 and later amendments cancel elected species as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder eligibility — claim must require all limitations of an allowable claim
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be eligible for rejoinder, a claim to a nonelected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim. A withdrawn claim that does not require all the limitations of an allowable claim will not be rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where restriction was between product and process and product is elected and allowable, all claims to nonelected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all limitations of an allowable claim to be eligible for rejoinder. Applicant is advised to amend nonelected claims during prosecution to require limitations of elected invention to retain right to rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoined claims must meet all patentability criteria and be fully examined
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104. Thus, to be allowable, the rejoined claims must meet all criteria for patentability including the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, and 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement for restriction between the rejoined inventions must be withdrawn. Reexamination may reveal rejoined claims unpatentable and may affect finality of office actions (see MPEP §706.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of restriction removes 35 U.S.C. 121 protection and can create double patenting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the restriction requirement is withdrawn, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable. Claims in a divisional that are anticipated by or include all limitations of an allowable claim in the parent may be subject to double patenting rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Ziegler and MPEP §804.01. Advise applicants that divisional claims may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections over claims of the instant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: C* classification reconsideration upon rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon rejoinder of a nonelected invention, the assigned examiner should reconsider whether the C* classification picture is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner believes C* classification is incorrect, enter a C* classification challenge at time of rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder between product inventions or between process inventions — withdraw restriction when claims require all limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction was required between independent or distinct products, or between independent or distinct processes, and all claims directed to an elected invention are allowable, the examiner should withdraw any restriction requirement between the elected invention and any nonelected invention that depends from or otherwise requires all the limitations of an allowable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that require all limitations of an allowable claim will be rejoined and fully examined. Claims that do not will remain withdrawn from consideration. Once restriction withdrawn, 35 U.S.C.121 no longer applies; double patenting considerations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments presenting additional dependent claims entered as matter of right if earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting additional claims that depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim will be entered as a matter of right if the amendment is presented prior to final rejection or allowance, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments submitted after final rejection are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; after allowance by 37 CFR 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.45 — Elected invention allowable; rejoin all previously withdrawn claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all claims to nonelected inventions depend from or require all limitations of an allowable claim, notify applicant that restriction requirement is withdrawn and previously withdrawn claims are rejoined and will be fully examined under 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert identification of rejoined claims and advise applicant divisional claims anticipated by or including limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional double patenting rejections. Use 8.43 instead where elected invention is product and previously nonelected process claims are rejoined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.49 — Elected invention allowable; claims stand withdrawn (restriction maintained)
rubrics_metrics.description: When elected invention is allowable but nonelected claims do not require all limitations of an allowable claim, the restriction requirement is maintained and the nonelected claims remain withdrawn from further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph to explain why nonelected claims are still withdrawn. Use alternative paragraphs if nonelected claims have been canceled or if restriction is withdrawn in whole/part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.50 — Elected invention allowable; partial withdrawal/partial rejoin
rubrics_metrics.description: If some nonelected claims require all limitations of an allowable claim and others do not, withdraw restriction as to claims that require all limitations and maintain it for others; notify applicant which claims are rejoined and which remain withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which groups/species are affected, whether withdrawal is full or partial, and the dates. Advise about double patenting consequences for divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of nonelected claims by applicant — reinstatement by timely amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonelected claims which depended from or required all limitations of an allowable claim were canceled by applicant, the canceled claim(s) may be reinstated by applicant if submitted in a timely filed amendment in reply to the action. Upon entry, such amended claim(s) will be examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.46, 8.47 or 8.47.01 as appropriate depending on timing (before final rejection, after final rejection, other outstanding issues). Time windows (e.g., two months) apply; if no timely amendment, application may be passed to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate form paragraph depending on timing and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose among form paragraphs (8.45, 8.46, 8.47, 8.47.01, 8.49, 8.50, etc.) depending on whether all/part/none of nonelected claims are rejoined, whether they were canceled by applicant, and whether the application is before or after final rejection/allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Examiner Notes in each form paragraph for bracket insertions and for special cases (e.g., AE program, product/process distinctions). Use 8.26 for non-responsive amendments; 8.26.AE for accelerated examination special status.
